According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple was reportedly once considering adding a feature to the Apple Upgrade Programme that would make setting up a new phone almost seamless: having your data pre-copied over by Apple in advance. However, the feature ultimately never came to fruition.

The idea was simple: since users upgrade their device on a fixed monthly payment plan every so often, why not make the transition as painless as possible? Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports as follows:

The idea obviously has a few flaws. Firstly, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, as the data transfer could only take place when the device is shipped, leaving a gap of a few days – unless you choose to pick it up in person at a store.

On top of that, there are privacy concerns that cannot be ignored. That said, if you already use iCloud backup on a regular basis, the fact that Apple holds your data is hardly surprising. But for the general public, how data is transferred to a new phone may raise concerns, with users potentially questioning whether anyone peeks at the information during the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a new system in its stores called Presto, which allows staff to update an iPhone while it is still in its box. One can imagine this system could in future be extended to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one needing to handle your data at any point.

That said, the feature never launched, and perhaps that is for the best.
